extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners preparing or prosecuting reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for preparing, filing, examining, and correcting amendments, claims, drawings, and certificates of correction in patent reissue applications under 37 CFR and relevant statutes (35 U.S.C.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for amendments (underlining and brackets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Underlining indicates added subject matter; brackets indicate deleted subject matter. If a claim is amended pursuant to paragraph (b)(2)(i)(A), a parenthetical expression 'amended,' 'twice amended,' etc., should follow the original claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.121(b)(1)(iii) and (b)(2)(i)(A) define markings. All bracketing and underlining is made in comparison to the original patent, not in comparison to the prior amendment. When printed, underlined matter appears in italics and brackets show deletions. Use double brackets/double underlining to distinguish prior reexamination/reissue changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of rewritten paragraphs for specification amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments including deletions or additions to the specification must be made by submission of a copy of each rewritten paragraph with markings (brackets and underlining). An entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presentation of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 37 CFR 1.121(b)(1)(i). All paragraphs added should be submitted as completely underlined. Present each rewritten paragraph as a complete unit; do not attempt partial-line markup of existing printed pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate precise point of each amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The precise point where each amendment is made must be indicated by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required by 37 CFR 1.121(b)(1)(ii). Use the paragraph location (e.g., column and line) or blocked paragraph/caret notation to show insertion points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present entire text of amended claims with markings
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim being amended by the submission, the entire text of the claim must be presented with markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required by 37 CFR 1.121(b)(2)(i)(A). Do not submit only the changed words; present the full claim with underlining/bracketing relative to the original patent claim text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For each new claim added by the amendment, the entire text of the added claim must be presented and completely underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required by 37 CFR 1.121(b)(2)(i)(B). New claims (not in the original patent) must be fully underlined to indicate added matter to the original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of claims by direction
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent claim should be canceled by a direction to cancel that claim; there is no need to present the patent claim surrounded by brackets. The same applies to canceling a new claim previously added in the reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.121(b)(2)(i)(C) and (D). Use explicit 'Cancel claim X.' statements rather than bracketing canceled claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not renumber original patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims must not be renumbered; a claim retains its original number even if canceled in the reissue proceeding. Numbering of any added claims must begin after the last original patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.121(b)(2)(i)(B). If new claims added during prosecution are later canceled, remaining new claims will be renumbered in sequence following the original patent claim count at allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set forth claim status with each amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendment submission must set forth the status (pending or canceled) as of the date of the amendment of all patent claims and of all added claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required by 37 CFR 1.121(b)(2)(ii). Failure to state claim status will generally result in notification that the amendment prior to final rejection is not completely responsive; after final rejection such amendment will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of support for claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim amendment must be accompanied by an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the amendment (support for insertions and deletions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required by 37 CFR 1.121(b)(2)(iii). Failure to provide explanation will generally result in non-entry before final rejection; such amendment after final rejection will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendments via new sheets only
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to original patent drawings are not permitted; any change must be made by filing a new sheet of drawings with amended figures identified as 'amended' and added figures as 'new'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.121(b)(3). See also MPEP § 1413. If desired, a sketch in permanent ink showing proposed changes in red may be filed for examiner approval and should be separate paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must not introduce new matter or be in expired patents
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may introduce new matter, and no amendment may be made in an expired patent. No reissue may enlarge the scope of the claims unless applied for within two years from the grant of the original patent (35 U.S.C. 251).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.121 and 35 U.S.C. 251. See MPEP § 1412.03 for time limitation on enlarging scope. If amendments would constitute new matter, reissue is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: All amendments made relative to patent as of reissue filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments must be made relative to the patent specification (including claims and drawings) which is in effect as of the date of filing of the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.121(b)(6). If there was a prior change to the patent (prior reexamination, prior reissue, certificate of correction), the first amendment must be made relative to the patent as changed; subsequent amendments must still be made vis-a-vis the patent specification in effect as of filing, not relative to the prior amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to formulas/equations when original has markup
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original patent includes a formula or equation already having underlining or bracketing as part of the formula, the entire formula should be bracketed and rewritten totally underlined in the re-presented paragraph; do not amend segments of a formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use double brackets and double underlining if the original includes prior bracketing/underlining to distinguish present changes. The reissue printed output will use double brackets and boldface for such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of blocked inserted paragraphs and caret notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inserted text in the specification is presented as blocked additions (assigned a letter and number) and a caret in the specification papers indicates where the blocked paragraph is to be incorporated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids page formatting concerns: applicants need not be concerned with physical insertion into existing page layout since blocked paragraphs are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper format examples for specification and claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Example formats: replace a paragraph by providing full paragraph with underlining/bracketing and point out location (e.g., 'Replace the paragraph beginning at column 4, line 23 with the following: ...'); for claim amendment present entire claim with underlining/bracketing and show dependency changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided examples: 'Claim 6 (Amended). The apparatus of claim [5] 1 wherein the [first] second...' ; when changing dependencies it's proper to make an original claim dependent upon a later-filed higher-numbered claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of claims: explicit written directive required
rubrics_metrics.description: To cancel an original patent claim or a new claim previously added in the reissue, direct cancellation in writing, e.g., 'Cancel claim 6.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Examples (3) and (4). Do not present canceled claims in brackets as a substitute for the written direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and numbering of new claims at allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: New claims added should be completely underlined and numbered beginning with the number next higher than the number of claims in the original patent. At allowance, remaining new claims additional to the patent claims should be renumbered in sequence starting with the number next higher than original patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if original claims were canceled, original numbering does not change. Examiner will renumber remaining new claims at allowance if some new claims were canceled during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of 'new claims' (previously added) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment of a 'new claim' must present the amended 'new claim' containing the amendatory material and completely underlining the claim; the presentation cannot contain bracketing or other indication of what was in the previous version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must point out what is changed in the 'Remarks' portion of the amendment. Each change must be accompanied by an explanation of the support in the disclosure as required by 37 CFR 1.121(b)(2)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple amendments to original patent claims (subsequent amendments must include prior changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending an original patent claim more than once, the later amendment must include the changes previously presented in earlier amendments (i.e., the later amendment's full claim text must reflect both prior and new changes relative to the original patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletions in earlier amendments that were not part of the original patent should not be shown in brackets in later amendments; they are simply omitted. Explanations of deletions or changes should appear in the remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief claim presentation for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims on appeal in a reissue application should include all underlining and bracketing necessary to reflect the changes made to the patent claims during prosecution; any new claims added should be completely underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 CFR 1.192 and MPEP § 1206 rules; present claims on appeal in the same manner they would be printed with reissue markings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure specification and amendments are in proper form for printing
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should ensure the specification is in proper form for printing: matter omitted by reissue enclosed in heavy brackets and matter added underlined (printed in italics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.173 and MPEP § 1411. Check entry of all amendments to ensure changes directed by applicant will be accurately printed in the reissue patent. Material added and later canceled should be crossed through, not bracketed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim designated for Official Gazette printing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one claim of an allowable reissue application must be designated for printing in the Official Gazette and must include a claim changed or added by the reissue; a canceled claim is not to be designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no change in claims or only cancellations, designate the most representative pending allowed claim for printing in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners may request proper formatted copy or prepare minor bracketed inserts
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reissue application is not prepared in the indicated manner, the examiner may request a clean copy of the reissue specification prepared in the indicated form; if deletions are small, examiner can prepare for issue by inserting bracketed inserts at appropriate places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examiner discretion to request corrected format or to prepare minimal formatting corrections when practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment and supplemental declaration procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may request applicant provide amendments or may make amendments with applicant's approval by a formal examiner's amendment; formal examiner's amendments must present the entire paragraphs or claims being amended in rewritten form for any deletions or additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner's amendment must comply with 37 CFR 1.121(b). If amendment is to correct an 'error' under 35 U.S.C. 251 and place application in condition for allowance, a supplemental oath or declaration will be required (see MPEP § 1444). Examiner should telephone applicant and request the supplemental oath/declaration prior to allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application monitoring and SPRE review flags
rubrics_metrics.description: All reissue applications are monitored and reviewed by the Office of the Special Program Examiner (SPRE) at several stages; SPRE must set terminal-specific PALM flags when a reissue enters the Examining Group and before a Notice of Allowance to ensure SPRE awareness and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags ensure SPRE can instruct examiner on reissue-specific procedures and conduct final review of reissue application, including screening for compliance with 37 CFR 1.175 (oath/declaration), presentation/entry of amendments (37 CFR 1.121(b)), and sample patentability review by Office of Patent Quality Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reissue on original patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issue of the reissued patent the surrender of the original patent takes effect, and the reissued patent has same effect in law as if originally granted in the amended form; however, where claims are identical, reissue does not affect pending actions or abate causes of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 35 U.S.C. 252 and MPEP discussion: reissue treated as if original patent had been granted in amended form; courts may provide equitable terms for continued manufacture/use where preparations were made prior to grant of reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of Correction for Office mistake (35 U.S.C. 254 / 37 CFR 1.322)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a mistake in a patent incurred through the fault of the Patent and Trademark Office is clearly disclosed by Office records, the Commissioner may issue a certificate of correction stating the fact and nature of such mistake (without charge) or issue a corrected patent in lieu thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.322. If certificate is inappropriate, Commissioner may issue corrected patent. Letters merely calling attention to errors will not be acknowledged. Request certificates only for errors of consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Correction for applicant's mistake (35 U.S.C. 255 / 37 CFR 1.323)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a mistake of a clerical/typographical nature or of minor character not the fault of the Office appears in a patent and showing is made that it occurred in good faith, the Commissioner may, upon payment of required fee, issue a certificate if the correction does not constitute new matter or require reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.323. The fee is set in 37 CFR 1.20(a) (except inventorship correction fees under 1.20(b)). Mistakes affecting claim scope typically require reissue rather than certificate of correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory criteria for applicant's certificate of correction (In re Arnott)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two requirements: (1) the mistake must be clerical, typographical, or of minor character; and (2) the proposed correction must not constitute new matter or require reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From In re Arnott, 19 USPQ2d 1049 (Comm'r Pat. 1991) as cited in MPEP. A mistake is not 'minor' if the requested change would materially affect scope or meaning of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of assignee's name procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment data on the Issue Fee Transmittal Form (PTOL-85B) should be completed; if assignee name is incomplete/erroneous on PTOL-85B, a request for certificate of correction will not be granted unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition under 1.183 must include the petition fee (1.17(h)), request that 37 CFR 3.81(a) be waived to permit correct assignee name after issuance, statement that failure was inadvertent, and copy of Notice of Recordation of Assignment Document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventors' names (35 U.S.C. 256 / 37 CFR 1.324)
rubrics_metrics.description: When through error a person is named or omitted as inventor and error arose without deceptive intention, the Commissioner may, on application of all parties and assignees with proof, issue a certificate correcting the inventorship; court-ordered corrections are also accommodated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.324 requires petitions be accompanied by statements from each person being added/deleted that the error occurred without deceptive intention, and statements from current named inventors either agreeing to the change or stating no disagreement. For court orders, submit copy of court order and certificate of correction to Certificates of Corrections Branch.
